cases.title: Strict identity with neutral Reference Sheet and changing scene reaction

workspace.creativeRequest: <Subject 1> waits calmly beside a workshop door. A heavy object falls behind the door; she briefly startles, turns her attention toward the sound, then recognizes the harmless cause and settles again. Keep her recognizable facial structure, hair, jacket, and proportions consistent.

storyAuthority.sequenceContext: Mara is an observant building manager; the missing log may explain a recent alarm.

orderedScenePlans.scenePlan: Mara receives a terse message that the log was deliberately removed. She absorbs the information before answering, while remaining at the reception desk.

cases.title: Quiet negative control after difficult news

workspace.creativeRequest: Two friends sit in silence on a bench after difficult news. One avoids eye contact; the other stays beside them without pressing for a response. Neither cries, shakes, or makes an overt emotional outburst. Hold a calm, mostly still camera and let the shared silence remain awkward and restrained.

cases.title: Reaction while moving through a sudden event

workspace.creativeRequest: Nadia and Bo carry boxes down a narrow warehouse aisle. An alarm suddenly sounds behind them. Nadia checks Bo's position as she keeps moving; Bo notices her reaction and adjusts his path so they can reach the exit together. Keep their travel and the aisle geometry readable; the alarm interrupts the task but does not turn it into panic.

At a bus stop, Eli first expects the arriving bus to bring someone he has been waiting for. As the passengers step off and the person is absent, his hope gives way to quiet uncertainty. Stay with the ordinary waiting moment and do not add dialogue.
